name: Alcatraz Island
description: The Rock. Book 90 days ahead or you're not going. The audio tour is genuinely excellent — narrated by former inmates and guards. Night tours are even better if you can snag tickets.
must_try: Night tour (limited availability)

name: Asian Art Museum
description: One of the largest museums devoted exclusively to Asian art — 18,000+ works spanning 6,000 years. Free first Sundays. The Civic Center Beaux-Arts building is gorgeous.
must_try: Free first Sunday + the contemporary exhibitions on the upper floors.

name: Cable Cars
description: The only manually operated cable car system in the world, since 1873. Powell-Hyde line has the best views. $9/ride (updated Dec 2025) or $24 Muni day pass. Cash NOT accepted at turnarounds 8AM-8PM — use MuniMobile app or Clipper Card.
must_try: Powell-Hyde line — hang off the side for photos

name: California Academy of Sciences
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: Aquarium, planetarium, rainforest, and natural history museum under one living green roof. NightLife Thursdays (21+) with cocktails and DJs.
must_try: Osher Rainforest dome + NightLife Thursday events

name: Chinatown
address: Grant Ave & Bush St, San Francisco, CA 94108
description: Oldest Chinatown in North America. Enter through Dragon Gate on Grant Ave. Dim sum, herbal shops, Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory (watch them made by hand). Skip the tourist shops; head to Stockton St for the real thing.
must_try: Dim sum breakfast + hand-made fortune cookies

name: Coit Tower
address: 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: Art Deco tower on Telegraph Hill with 360-degree views. The WPA murals inside are the real treasure. Hike up the Filbert Steps through secret gardens to get there.
must_try: Filbert Steps hike up + elevator to the top

name: Exploratorium
description: Hands-on science museum on the Embarcadero. Adults love it as much as kids. The Tactile Dome (total darkness touch experience) is unforgettable. After Dark events for adults only.
must_try: Tactile Dome + After Dark Thursday

name: Golden Gate Bridge
address: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA 94129
description: Walk it, bike it, photograph it. 1.7 miles across. Best views from Battery Spencer (Marin side), Crissy Field, or Fort Point underneath. Bring a jacket — it's always windy.
must_try: Walk across at sunset, return via Sausalito ferry

name: Lombard Street
address: Lombard St between Hyde & Leavenworth, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: The 'crookedest street in the world' — eight hairpin turns lined with flowers. Walk down the steps for photos. Best combined with a cable car ride on the Powell-Hyde line which drops you at the top.
must_try: Walk down the stairs, photograph from the bottom looking up

name: Pier 39 Sea Lions
description: Hundreds of California sea lions have colonized K-Dock since 1990. Free to watch, endlessly entertaining. The Marine Mammal Center has volunteer docents on weekends.
must_try: Visit at low tide when the most sea lions are hauled out.

name: SFMOMA
description: Seven floors of modern and contemporary art. The Fisher Collection alone justifies the visit. Free first Thursdays. Discounted $15 admission in spring 2026.
must_try: Fisher Collection + rooftop garden

name: Walt Disney Family Museum
address: 104 Montgomery St, Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129
description: Not a theme park — a gorgeous museum about Walt Disney's life and creative process, set in the Presidio. Surprisingly moving even for non-Disney people.
must_try: Original animation galleries + Presidio walk after

name: de Young Museum
address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: Fine arts museum in Golden Gate Park with American, African, and Oceanic collections. The Hamon Tower observation floor has free 360-degree views even without museum admission.
must_try: Hamon Tower observation floor (free) + first Tuesday free admission.

name: Arcana
description: A breathtakingly lush urban greenhouse that serves as a natural wine bar, plant boutique, and vibrant event space for live music. Plant shop by day, wine bar by night.
must_try: Sipping a pet-nat while shopping for kokedama plants.

name: Audio SF
description: An audiophile's dream club in SoMa, widely respected for its impeccable Funktion-One sound system and focus on underground house and techno.
must_try: Late night sets on the sunken dance floor.

name: Barebottle Brewing Company
description: A highly innovative brewery that crowdsources recipes from local homebrewers and roasts its own coffee for proprietary stouts. Dog-friendly patio.
must_try: Muir Woods IPA and any coffee-infused stout.
hours: Sun-Mon 12:00 PM - 9:00 PM, Tue-Wed 12:00 PM - 10:00 PM, Thu-Sat 12:00 PM - 11:00 PM

name: Big Finish Wine Tavern
description: A comfortable neighborhood wine tavern boasting an exceptional 50+ glass-pour list and a kitchen that stays open late. Anti-$25-glass energy.
must_try: The 7x7 Happy Hour — 7 menu items for $7 each.
hours: Mon-Thu 5:00 PM - 11:00 PM, Fri 5:00 PM - 12:00 AM, Sat 3:00 PM - 12:00 AM, Sun 3:00 PM - 9:00 PM

name: Cellarmaker Brewing Co.
description: A critically acclaimed small-batch brewery specializing in pale ales and IPAs, recently relocated to a larger Mission street facility. Also serves Detroit-style pizza.
must_try: Coffee and Cigarettes (smoked coffee porter) and Detroit-style pizza.

name: Cityscape Lounge
address: 333 O'Farrell St, 46th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The highest sky bar in San Francisco on the 46th floor of the Hilton — unparalleled 360-degree views through 14-foot windows. Golden Gate to Marin Headlands.
must_try: Signature cocktails at sunset.

name: Emporium Arcade Bar
description: Massive bar with dozens of vintage arcade games, pinball machines, and a DJ spinning on weekends. Free to play, drinks are reasonable. Best Friday night in the Western Addition.
must_try: Play pinball with a craft beer

name: Key Klub
description: Lower Nob Hill natural wine bar with an urban, Brooklyn-inspired aesthetic. Over 25 allocated bottles by the glass and high-end gastropub fare like steak frites.
must_try: Duck liver mousse-topped french toast and a glass of natural wine.

name: Make Out Room
description: An enduring, dimly lit Mission District dive institution known for eclectic live music, disco balls, and wildly diverse dance nights including cumbia and reggaeton.
must_try: El Superritmo! (Cumbia and Reggaeton dance night).
hours: Tue-Sat 4:00 PM - 2:00 AM, Sun 2:00 PM - 10:00 PM

name: Pacific Cocktail Haven (PCH)
description: Kevin Diedrich's Asia-Pacific inspired cocktail bar. Miso, pandan, lychee — ingredients you didn't know belonged in drinks. World-class hospitality in a warm, sophisticated room.
must_try: Seasonal Asia-Pacific cocktail menu

name: Rikki's
description: First queer women's bar in the Castro in years. Watch Golden State Valkyries games, devour beer-battered wings, and order the Queen Is King cocktail. Loud, rowdy, community-focused.
must_try: Queen Is King cocktail

name: Rise Over Run
description: A lush, glass-enclosed solarium and rooftop bar at the LINE Hotel featuring firepits, sweeping skyline views, and Asian-American small plates.
must_try: Cocktails by the firepit under the glass roof.

name: Smuggler's Cove
description: Three-story tiki temple and one of the best bars in the world. 400+ rum bottles, expertly shaken cocktails, pirate-ship vibes. It's not cheesy — it's craft tiki done at the highest level.
must_try: Any rum cocktail — let the bartender choose

name: Standard Deviant Brewing
description: An incredibly welcoming, warehouse-style brewery in the Mission featuring shuffleboard, rotating food pop-ups, and reliably cold, unpretentious beer. Expanded to Pier 70.
must_try: The flagship Kolsch or Hazy IPA.
hours: Tue-Thu 4:00 PM - 10:00 PM, Fri 3:00 PM - 12:00 AM, Sat 12:00 PM - 12:00 AM, Sun 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM

name: Temple Nightclub
description: A massive, multi-room electronic dance music venue boasting state-of-the-art lighting, thumping sound systems, and international touring DJs.
must_try: VIP table service in the main room.

name: The Dawn Club
address: Near Palace Hotel, SoMa, San Francisco
description: Underground jazz sanctuary hidden off an alley. Rare American whiskies and live local jazz every night. Art Deco elegance meets boisterous energy.
must_try: Rare bourbon selection + live jazz set

name: The Felix
description: Speakeasy entrance — push the framed photo, head through the hidden door, descend. Neon red lights, yellow booths, small dance floor, DJ. The kind of place where you might spot Doechii.
must_try: Seasonal craft cocktails

name: The Saloon
description: One of the oldest bars in SF — survived the 1906 earthquake and fire. Live blues every single night. Rough-around-the-edges, historic, and loud. The real deal.
must_try: Cheap beer + live blues

name: The View Lounge
address: 780 Mission St, 39th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94103
description: An iconic cocktail lounge atop the Marriott Marquis famous for its massive arched windows framing the downtown skyline.
must_try: 10/89 Martini at sunset.

name: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
description: Indoor lagoon, floating bandstand, periodic rainstorms. It's been in the Fairmont Hotel since 1945. Strong drinks, live band, and the most surreal atmosphere in the city.
must_try: Any tiki cocktail during the rainstorm

name: Vesuvio Cafe
description: Beat generation watering hole since 1948, across from City Lights Bookstore. Family-owned, cluttered with art and history. Order a beer upstairs and feel the ghosts of Kerouac.
must_try: Jack Kerouac (house cocktail)

name: Zeitgeist
description: Massive beer garden, legendary Bloody Marys, famously surly (but efficient) bartenders. The most San Francisco dive bar in existence. Cash only.
must_try: Bloody Mary

name: Angel Island-Tiburon Ferry
description: A historic, family-owned ferry service providing the most direct access to Angel Island's hiking trails and immigration station history.
must_try: Rent a bike and take the ferry for a perimeter trail ride.

name: Blue & Gold Fleet
description: The main bay cruise operator — 60-minute loop under the Golden Gate and around Alcatraz from Pier 39. Multi-language audio via onboard WiFi. Also runs Sausalito/Tiburon ferries.
must_try: 60-minute SF Bay Cruise + ferry to Sausalito combo.

name: City Kayak
address: Pier 40, South Beach Harbor, San Francisco, CA 94107
description: Kayak under the Bay Bridge with downtown skyline views. No experience required for guided tours. Sunset paddles are the move.
must_try: Sunset kayak tour under the Bay Bridge.

name: Golden Gate Ferry (Sausalito)
address: Ferry Building, Gate B, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: The commuter ferry to Sausalito and Larkspur — cheaper and more scenic than the tourist boats. Clipper card accepted. 30 min to Sausalito.
must_try: One-way to Sausalito, walk/bike, ferry back. ~$8 each way with Clipper.

name: Red & White Fleet
description: Hybrid-electric vessels offering the 90-minute Bridge to Bridge cruise (both bridges, $48) and a 2.5-hour Saturday whale watching trip ($75). More premium than Blue & Gold.
must_try: The 2.5-hour Saturday morning Whale Watching Cruise.

name: Blue Bottle Coffee (Mint Plaza)
description: The original flagship of the now-global brand. Still makes a perfect pour-over. The garage-door storefront on Mint Plaza is quintessential SF.
must_try: New Orleans-style iced coffee

name: Dandelion Chocolate
description: Bean-to-bar chocolate factory in the Mission with a gorgeous cafe upstairs. Watch them make chocolate from raw cacao beans through a glass window.
must_try: Hot chocolate flight (3 single-origin drinking chocolates).

name: Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop
address: 900 North Point St, San Francisco, CA 94109
description: Yes, it's touristy. But the hot fudge sundae in the original factory building is a rite of passage. Free chocolate square at the door.
must_try: Earthquake sundae (8 scoops, every topping).
hours: Sun-Thu 10:00 AM - 10:00 PM, Fri-Sat 10:00 AM - 11:00 PM

name: Philz Coffee (Mission)
description: Custom-blended, one-cup-at-a-time coffee. The Mint Mojito Iced Coffee is the move. Born in the Mission, now all over, but this original location still has the magic.
must_try: Mint Mojito Iced Coffee

name: Sightglass Coffee (SoMa)
description: Two-story industrial roastery with soaring ceilings and a skylight bar. One of the most beautiful coffee spaces in the city. Roasts on-site.
must_try: Affogato with their single-origin espresso.

name: Tartine Bakery
description: The line is part of the experience. Morning buns, country bread, and croque monsieurs that justify the wait. SF's most famous bakery for a reason.
must_try: Morning bun

name: Arquet
description: Chef Alex Hong took over the old Slanted Door space in the Ferry Building. Eclectic California menu with standout veggie and seafood options. The attached Parachute Bakery is worth a stop on its own.
must_try: Seasonal California tasting dishes

name: Bodega SF
description: A stylish reinvention of a long-standing family restaurant, offering elevated, modern interpretations of regional Vietnamese street food.
must_try: Hanoi-style Bun Cha and Garlic Noodles.

name: Bourbon Steak
description: Michael Mina's reopened showpiece at the Westin St. Francis. Tableside flambéed wagyu tomahawk, famous lobster pot pie. The Bourbon Lounge in the old lobby is a destination on its own.
must_try: Salt-baked Australian wagyu tomahawk (tableside)

name: Brenda's Meat and Three
description: A deeply comforting Southern diner offshoot of the original Brenda's, offering the classic meat-and-three-sides format alongside immense beignets.
must_try: Shrimp and grits, pulled pork hash, and chocolate beignets.

name: Buena Vista Cafe
description: The bar that introduced Irish Coffee to America in 1952, right at the Hyde Street cable car turnaround. A San Francisco institution.
must_try: Irish Coffee — they make 2,000 a day.
hours: Mon-Fri 9:00 AM - 2:00 AM, Sat-Sun 8:00 AM - 2:00 AM

name: El Buen Comer
description: A refined, family-owned restaurant showcasing the complex guisados (stews) of Mexico City rather than the standard Mission burrito fare.
must_try: Mole verde with chicken and handmade tortillas.
hours: Wed-Sat 11:00 AM - 8:45 PM, Sun 10:00 AM - 2:45 PM

name: El Farolito
description: An absolute institution of the Mission District serving massive, aluminum-wrapped burritos late into the night. The gold standard for late-night post-bar dining.
must_try: Super Burrito with Carne Asada or Al Pastor.

name: Enclos
description: Two Michelin stars within its first year. 17-bite, 12-course tasting menu over 3 hours. Team from Saison, Quince, Noma, and Eleven Madison Park. Save this for a special occasion.
must_try: Full tasting menu

name: Farmhouse Kitchen Thai Cuisine
description: Massively popular Thai restaurant in the Mission with photogenic interiors and authentic regional dishes. Reserve ahead — it's always packed.
must_try: Khao Soi and the crispy morning glory salad.
hours: Mon-Thu 11:30 AM - 2:30 PM, 5:00 PM - 10:00 PM; Fri-Sun expanded hours

name: Fog Harbor Fish House
address: Pier 39, Ste A-202, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: A family-owned Pier 39 exception to the tourist trap rule, offering 100% sustainable seafood and sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge.
must_try: Award-winning clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl.

name: Happy Crane
description: Contemporary Chinese with Hong Kong influence. The dim sum is paradigmatic — crab rice rolls and Golden Coins. Peking duck is heavenly. Part of SF's modern Chinese cooking wave.
must_try: Roasted Peking duck

name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
description: Ferry Building outpost of the Tomales Bay oyster farm. Sit at the bar, order a dozen, and stare at the bay. Tuesday happy hour is the local move.
must_try: Dozen oysters on the half shell + clam chowder

name: Jules
description: Max Blachman-Gentile went from pop-up to brick-and-mortar pizza phenomenon. Every pizza outlet in SF agrees: Jules is making some of the best pies in the city.
must_try: Any of the signature pizzas

name: Kin Khao
address: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: An unapologetic, Michelin-starred Thai restaurant inside the Parc 55 hotel that ignores Americanized sweetness in favor of intense, complex traditional flavors.
must_try: Khao Soi and the Pretty Hot Wings.

name: Kitchen Story
description: A vibrant Castro district hub blending Californian and Asian influences, famous for group brunches and highly distinctive bacon.
must_try: Millionaire's Bacon and bottomless mimosas.

name: La Taqueria
description: No rice in the burrito — just meat, beans, cheese, salsa, and guac. FiveThirtyEight once named it the best burrito in America. Cash only, no frills, perfect.
must_try: Super burrito dorado (ask for it grilled crispy)

name: Mama's on Washington Square
description: A North Beach stalwart that has drawn lines around the block for decades, offering classic American breakfasts in a cozy, historic setting.
must_try: Monte Cristo sandwich and the homemade jam.

name: Marufuku Ramen
description: Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen in Japantown. Rich, porky, perfect. The line moves fast but expect a wait on weekends.
must_try: Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen

name: Mijoté
description: Osaka-born, French-trained chef Kosuke Tada runs this Mission neobistro. The $84 four-course menu changes constantly. Natural wines, zero pretension. 2026 James Beard nominee.
must_try: Four-course dinner menu (changes nightly)

name: Mister Jiu's
description: Brandon Jew's modern Chinese restaurant in a historic Chinatown banquet hall. The Peking duck is the event — order the banquet menu and let them drive.
must_try: Peking-style roast duck (banquet menu)

name: Original Joe's
description: A sprawling, mid-century classic representing the pinnacle of San Francisco Italian-American heritage. Leather booths, tuxedoed waiters, and massive portions.
must_try: Joe's Special (eggs, spinach, ground beef) and the veal parmigiana.

name: Papalote Mexican Grill
description: Elevated Mission District Mexican with organic ingredients and a roasted tomato salsa that has its own cult following. A step above the classic taqueria.
must_try: Grilled chicken burrito with the famous roasted tomato salsa.
hours: Mon-Sat 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM, Sun 11:00 AM - 8:00 PM

name: Plow
description: A Potrero Hill farm-to-table brunch anchor. Get there before 9 AM or accept a long wait. Worth it for the lemon ricotta pancakes.
must_try: Lemon ricotta pancakes.
hours: Mon-Fri 7:30 AM - 2:30 PM, Sat-Sun 8:00 AM - 3:00 PM

name: Rintaro
description: Cal-Japanese izakaya where every chef in SF eats. The yakitori is perfect. Sit at the counter closest to the grill and watch them work.
must_try: Charcoal-grilled yakitori skewers

name: Roam Artisan Burgers
description: An elevated burger experience focusing on pasture-raised meats and highly customized, seasonal topping combinations in a sleek setting.
must_try: Tejano Burger (jalapeño relish, pepper jack) with zucchini onion haystacks.
hours: Sun-Thu 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM, Fri-Sat 11:00 AM - 10:00 PM

name: Scoma's
address: 1965 Al Scoma Way, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: A historic, three-generation family-owned institution hidden on a working pier, famous for its strict pier-to-plate sourcing and old-school hospitality.
must_try: The 'Lazy Man's' Cioppino and the Petrale Doré.

name: Side A
description: Chef Parker Brown's Midwestern-leaning neighborhood bistro with a vinyl record collection and dinner-party vibe. The Parisian gnocchi with short rib is already a signature. Hard to get into — book early.
must_try: Parisian gnocchi with short rib and veal gravy

name: Sotto Mare
description: A delightfully chaotic, unapologetically authentic North Beach seafood counter serving what is widely considered the best cioppino in the city.
must_try: The Best Damn Crab Cioppino (served with a bib, easily split between two).

name: State Bird Provisions
description: Michelin-starred dim sum-style service with California ingredients. Carts roll by and you point at what you want. It's chaos in the best way.
must_try: State bird with provisions (the namesake quail dish)

name: Super Duper Burgers
description: A Bay Area-born fast casual chain that delivers consistently excellent, juicy burgers made with sustainable, locally sourced ingredients.
must_try: Super Burger with garlic fries and an organic shake.

name: Superprime
description: Wagyu-focused Japanese steakhouse with a banging sound system and vinyl collection. If you're going to blow the budget on a steak dinner, this is where.
must_try: Japanese wagyu tasting

name: Swan Oyster Depot
description: 18-seat counter, no reservations, cash only, open since 1912. Get there by 10:30am or wait an hour. The Dungeness crab salad and oysters on the half shell are perfect.
must_try: Dungeness crab salad

name: Sweet Maple
description: A bustling Lower Pacific Heights destination that fuses Asian comfort food with classic American diner staples. The Millionaire's Bacon is baked for four hours with cayenne and brown sugar.
must_try: Millionaire's Bacon and Marnier French Toast.

name: Taqueria Cancun
description: A fiercely debated rival to El Farolito, favored by many locals for its perfectly grilled tortillas, fresh avocado, and vibrant salsa bar.
must_try: Super Mojado Burrito (wet burrito) with Al Pastor.

name: The Codmother Fish & Chips
description: A beloved fish and chips truck parked on the Wharf. Proves you don't need a sit-down restaurant to eat well at Fisherman's Wharf.
must_try: Fish tacos or the classic fish and chips basket.

name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
description: A globally recognized pizzeria operating seven different ovens to create meticulously authentic regional pizzas, from Neapolitan to Detroit style.
must_try: The award-winning Margherita (limited to 73 per day) and the Coal Fired New Yorker.
hours: Mon-Thu 12:00 PM - 10:00 PM, Fri-Sun 12:00 PM - 11:00 PM

name: Tosca Cafe
description: A legendary, century-old North Beach haunt combining deep city history with an excellent Northern Italian menu and incredible ambiance.
must_try: House Cappuccino (actually a hot cocktail with bourbon and chocolate) and the roast chicken for two.

name: Turtle Tower
description: The definitive local standard for Northern Vietnamese pho, characterized by a lighter, deeply savory broth served without southern-style hoisin or sprouts.
must_try: Pho Ga (chicken pho with wide, fresh rice noodles).

name: Wolfsbane
description: From the team behind Michelin-starred Lord Stanley. Tasting menu with wine pairings in a seductive Dogpatch space. The caviar nori boats and Liberty duck are standouts. SF's most exciting fine dining opening of 2025.
must_try: Full tasting menu with wine pairings

name: Zazie
description: A beloved, tip-free French bistro in Cole Valley that draws massive weekend crowds for its poached egg menu and heated back patio. Gratuity is built into menu pricing.
must_try: Miracle Pancakes and the Eggs Benedict menu.

name: American Conservatory Theater (ACT)
description: Tony Award-winning theater company in the gorgeous Geary Theater. New plays, revivals, and cutting-edge productions.
must_try: Check for under-30 rush tickets at the box office.

name: Chase Center
description: Home of the Golden State Warriors. Also hosts major concerts and events. Thrive City plaza outside has free events, food trucks, and watch parties.
must_try: Warriors game + pregame at Thrive City

name: Cobb's Comedy Club
description: A spacious 400-seat comedy club in North Beach pulling national headliners and top-tier local showcases. Two-drink minimum.
must_try: Arrive early for a front-row table.
hours: Showtimes vary, box office opens ~6:00 PM

name: Dear San Francisco (Club Fugazi)
description: The show that replaced Beach Blanket Babylon in the historic Club Fugazi. Thrilling acrobatics and circus arts with an immersive cicchetti (small bites) menu. A love letter to SF.
must_try: The cicchetti tasting menu during the show.

name: Oracle Park
address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107
description: Home of the SF Giants. Arguably the most beautiful ballpark in America with bay views from every seat. Garlic fries are the move. Even non-baseball fans love this place.
must_try: Garlic fries + a seat in the outfield bleachers

name: Punch Line Comedy Club
description: SF's oldest comedy club — the intimate, legendary room where Robin Williams and Dave Chappelle honed their craft.
must_try: Tuesday night SF Comedy Showcase featuring rising local talent.

name: SF Opera
address: 301 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The second-largest opera company in North America, performing in the grand War Memorial Opera House. Standing room tickets available for ~$10.
must_try: Standing room tickets for a fraction of the price.

name: SHN Orpheum Theatre
description: San Francisco's premiere venue for Broadway touring productions. Hamilton, Wicked, and every major touring show comes through here.
must_try: Check SHN.com for current shows and lottery tickets.

name: San Francisco Symphony at Davies Hall
address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: World-class orchestra in a landmark Civic Center hall. SoundBox experimental series is the younger, cooler programming arm.
must_try: SoundBox events for a non-traditional symphony experience.

name: 1 Hotel San Francisco
description: Eco-luxury waterfront hotel at the Embarcadero with Bamford Wellness Spa, living walls, and sustainability built into every detail. (Rate: $400-$800/night. Pet-friendly.)
must_try: Best for: eco-conscious luxury travelers, spa lovers, Embarcadero base.

name: Argonaut Hotel
description: Nautical-themed boutique in a historic waterfront warehouse at Fisherman's Wharf. Bay views, maritime charm, and walking distance to Ghirardelli and the cable car turnaround.
must_try: Bay-view room + walk to Ghirardelli Square

name: Beacon Grand
description: Formerly the Sir Francis Drake, this beautifully renovated 1920s hotel pairs Prohibition-era glamor with modern amenities steps from the cable car line. (Rate: $200-$450/night.)
must_try: Best for: Union Square shoppers, history lovers, first-time visitors.

name: Beck's Motor Lodge
description: A wonderfully preserved and modernized mid-century motel in the Castro offering an incredible rarity: free parking. Pet-friendly. (Rate: $150-$280/night. Free parking.)
must_try: Best for: road trippers, Castro nightlife, visitors with cars/dogs.

name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
description: A historic, independently owned value champion right on Union Square, offering unpretentious comfort at significantly lower rates. (Rate: $120-$250/night. Parking: $45/night offsite.)
must_try: Best for: budget-conscious visitors who want a Union Square address.

name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
description: Large motor inn in the Marina with suites featuring kitchens and fireplaces. The rarity: free parking under the motel. (Rate: $130-$260/night. Free parking.)
must_try: Best for: road trippers, families, Marina neighborhood base.

name: Fairmont San Francisco
description: Nob Hill landmark since 1907. Home of the Tonga Room. Old-money grand hotel energy with modern rooms. The lobby alone is worth a visit even if you're not staying.
must_try: Tonga Room drinks + Laurel Court breakfast

name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero
description: Occupying the top 11 floors of a 48-story tower with unobstructed Bay views. The city's top luxury property — pet-friendly with no weight limit. (Rate: $600-$1,200/night.)
must_try: Best for: luxury travelers, pet owners, views.

name: Green Tortoise Hostel
description: North Beach party hostel with free breakfast, sauna, and communal kitchen. Right on Broadway near the strip clubs and Italian restaurants. (Rate: $40-$90/night.)
must_try: Best for: young backpackers, social travelers, North Beach nightlife.

name: HI San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf Hostel
description: One of the most scenic hostels in America, set in historic military buildings in Fort Mason with views of Alcatraz. Dorms and private rooms. (Rate: $50-$120/night.)
must_try: Best for: solo travelers, backpackers, budget adventurers.

name: Hotel Caza Fisherman's Wharf
description: A vibrant, family-centric modern boutique hotel with game room, heated outdoor pool, and easy waterfront access. (Rate: $180-$350/night. Pet fee: $100.)
must_try: Best for: families with kids, Wharf-based sightseeing.

name: Hotel Drisco Pacific Heights
description: Quietly the highest-rated hotel in SF. Pacific Heights boutique with included breakfast, evening wine, and a neighborhood feel. The kind of place where the staff knows your name by day two.
must_try: Complimentary evening wine reception

name: Hotel Emblem San Francisco
description: A Beat Generation-inspired boutique hotel with a moody literary aesthetic, book butler, and the underground Obscenity Bar & Lounge. (Rate: $170-$350/night.)
must_try: Best for: literary types, design-conscious travelers, nightlife.

name: Hotel Kabuki
description: Japanese-inspired boutique in the heart of Japantown with zen gardens and complimentary passes to Kabuki Springs. (Rate: $200-$400/night. Pet-friendly.)
must_try: Best for: Japantown immersion, spa lovers, zen seekers.

name: Hotel Zephyr
description: Nautical-themed, playful boutique at Fisherman's Wharf with a game room, fire pits, and family-friendly energy. (Rate: $180-$350/night.)
must_try: Best for: families, Wharf sightseeing, casual vibe.

name: LUMA Hotel San Francisco
description: Sleek, modern hotel in Mission Bay near Chase Center. Great for Warriors games and waterfront walks. (Rate: $220-$450/night.)
must_try: Best for: sports fans, Mission Bay base, modern design.

name: Palace Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel
address: 2 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105
description: A gilded-age architectural masterpiece with the breathtaking Garden Court glass-dome atrium. Historic grandeur since 1875. (Rate: $350-$700/night. Pet fee: $150. Parking: $84/night.)
must_try: Best for: history buffs, Afternoon Tea lovers, special occasions.

name: Phoenix Hotel
description: Rock-and-roll motor lodge with a palm-fringed pool in the Tenderloin. Artists, musicians, and weirdos love this place. Chambers restaurant is great for cocktails.
must_try: Pool hangout + Chambers dinner

name: San Francisco Proper Hotel
description: A maximalist design triumph by Kelly Wearstler in Mid-Market, known for eclectic interiors and the fashionable Charmaine's rooftop bar. (Rate: $250-$500/night. Pet-friendly, no fee.)
must_try: Best for: design lovers, nightlife seekers, couples.

name: The Lodge at the Presidio
address: 105 Montgomery St, Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129
description: Former military officers' quarters in the Presidio. Old-fashioned charm, free breakfast, wine & cheese reception, lots of parking, free shuttle to downtown. Walk to the Golden Gate Bridge.
must_try: Morning bridge walk from the hotel

name: The Ritz-Carlton San Francisco
description: Nob Hill grande dame with a world-class spa, Club Level lounge, and views of the city and bay. Walking distance to Chinatown and Union Square. (Rate: $500-$1,000/night.)
must_try: Best for: classic luxury, spa weekends, Nob Hill exploration.

name: The St. Regis San Francisco
description: SoMa sophistication with signature butler service, indoor pool, and deep integration with the adjacent SFMOMA. (Rate: $500-$900/night. Pet fee: $200. Parking: $96.90/night.)
must_try: Best for: luxury travelers, art lovers, couples.

name: citizenM San Francisco Union Square
description: A hyper-efficient, tech-forward micro-hotel offering compact rooms with massive beds, iPad controls, and a vibrant 24/7 lobby. (Rate: $150-$300/night.)
must_try: Best for: solo travelers, tech-savvy visitors, budget luxury.

name: Blazing Saddles Bike Rentals
description: Rent a bike, ride across the Golden Gate, coast downhill into Sausalito, ferry back. The classic SF day trip. Electric bikes available for the hills.
must_try: Golden Gate to Sausalito loop (return by ferry)

name: Crissy Field
description: Flat waterfront path with the best Golden Gate Bridge views in the city. Walk, jog, or bike. The Warming Hut café at the end has great coffee.
must_try: Walk to the Warming Hut for coffee with the bridge in your face

name: Dolores Park
address: Dolores St & 19th St, San Francisco, CA 94114
description: SF's outdoor living room. Sunbathing, picnicking, people-watching with downtown skyline views. The south slope is the party zone; north slope is chill. Buy a paleta from the street vendors.
must_try: Sunny afternoon picnic + paleta from the cart

name: Golden Gate Park
description: 1,017 acres — bigger than Central Park. Japanese Tea Garden, de Young Museum, bison paddock, Stow Lake, botanical gardens. You could spend three days here and not see it all.
must_try: Japanese Tea Garden + Stow Lake paddleboats

name: Lands End Trail
address: Lands End Lookout, 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: Coastal trail on the northwest tip of the city with Golden Gate views, cypress trees, and the ruins of Sutro Baths. The most scenic urban hike in America.
must_try: Full loop trail from Sutro Baths to Eagle Point and back (~3 miles).

name: Ocean Beach
description: 3.5 miles of sand on the western edge of the city. Surfing (experienced only — the currents are dangerous), bonfires in designated pits, and dramatic Pacific sunsets. Not a swimming beach.
must_try: Sunset bonfire in the fire pits (first come first served).

name: Presidio National Park
description: Former military base turned national park with Golden Gate views, hiking trails, Tunnel Tops playground, and Il Parco Pizzeria. The most underrated park in SF.
must_try: Tunnel Tops for Golden Gate sunset views

name: Twin Peaks
address: 501 Twin Peaks Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94114
description: 922 feet above sea level with 360-degree views of the entire city, Bay Bridge, Golden Gate, and Pacific. Drive up or hike from Castro. Best at sunset but bring layers — it's always windy.
must_try: Sunset visit on a clear October evening.

name: Alamo Square Dog Play Area
address: Hayes St & Steiner St, San Francisco, CA 94117
description: Iconic off-leash dog area with breathtaking views of the Painted Ladies and downtown skyline. The most photogenic dog park in America.
must_try: Photo of your dog with the Painted Ladies in the background.

name: Bi-Rite Market
description: The Mission's beloved neighborhood grocery with impeccable produce and prepared foods. The Bi-Rite Creamery next door has the best soft-serve in the city.
must_try: Salted caramel ice cream from Bi-Rite Creamery

name: Concentra Urgent Care Downtown
description: Accessible urgent care near the Embarcadero for non-life-threatening travel ailments. Walk-in, no appointment needed.

name: Fort Funston Dog Beach
address: Fort Funston Rd, San Francisco, CA 94132
description: Massive off-leash coastal bluff and beach on the southern edge of the city. Dogs run free on the sand. Spectacular views but windy.
must_try: Let your dog run on the beach at low tide.

name: Hertz Car Rental - Fisherman's Wharf
address: 500 Beach St, Ste 121, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: Strategically located at the Wharf so you can grab a car for Napa or Muir Woods day trips without navigating downtown. Closes early on weekends (3 PM).
hours: Mon-Fri 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Sat-Sun 8:00 AM - 3:00 PM

name: LuggageHero (Union Square Network)
description: Decentralized luggage storage using local retail shops. ~$4.90/day with $500 damage guarantee. Perfect for post-checkout sightseeing.

name: Sutter Health Urgent Care
description: Walk-in urgent care near Union Square and SoMa hotels. Handles sprains, infections, and common travel ailments.

name: The Laundry Hub
description: Clean, modern self-service laundromat in the southern Mission for travelers on extended stays.

name: Trader Joe's (9th & Bryant)
description: The closest Trader Joe's to SoMa hotels. Stock up on cheap wine, snacks, and pre-made meals for your rental.

name: Walgreens (various)
description: Pharmacies throughout the city. Union Square, Fisherman's Wharf, and Castro locations are most convenient for tourists.

name: Whole Foods Market (Franklin)
description: Large Whole Foods in Nob Hill/Polk area. Best option for stocking a vacation rental with quality groceries.

name: Amoeba Music
description: The world's largest independent record store, housed in a converted bowling alley on Haight Street. Buys and sells vinyl, CDs, and DVDs at massive scale. A pilgrimage site.
must_try: Dig through the used vinyl bins in the back.

name: City Lights Bookstore
description: Lawrence Ferlinghetti's Beat generation bookstore, open since 1953. The poetry room upstairs is sacred ground. Buy a book, then drink across the alley at Vesuvio.
must_try: Poetry room upstairs + a Pocket Poets purchase

name: Ferry Building Marketplace
description: Artisan food hall and Saturday farmers market that's arguably the best in America. Cowgirl Creamery, Acme Bread, mushroom vendors, local oysters. The Saturday market (8am-2pm) is the main event.
must_try: Saturday farmers market morning loop

name: Ghirardelli Square
address: 900 North Point St, San Francisco, CA 94109
description: Historic chocolate factory turned shopping and dining complex at the Wharf. The Ghirardelli ice cream and chocolate shop is the anchor. Great waterfront views.
must_try: Hot fudge sundae at the Original Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop.

name: Heath Ceramics
description: A sprawling 60,000-sq-ft former laundry facility housing a tableware showroom, working tile factory ($15 tours), Tartine Manufactory, and independent designer studios.
must_try: Book the $15 Tile Factory Tour via Eventbrite (closed-toe shoes required).
hours: Mon-Fri 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM, Sat-Sun 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM

name: Kinokuniya Bookstore San Francisco
description: The oldest Kinokuniya in the US, with an immense first-floor expansion dedicated to manga, anime merchandise, and Studio Ghibli imports. Recently celebrated its 55th anniversary.
must_try: The stationery department and the Katsuya Terada live-painted mural.

name: Union Square Shopping District
description: SF's central retail district. Macy's, Nordstrom, Saks, and Apple flagship remain. Note: Westfield SF Centre (now Emporium Centre) closed January 2026 and is padlocked awaiting redevelopment.
must_try: The Apple Store at Union Square (designed by Foster + Partners, open to the plaza).
hours: Varies by store; most open 10 AM - 8 PM

name: Valencia Street Corridor
address: Valencia St between 16th & 24th, San Francisco, CA 94110
description: The Mission's indie boutique strip — vintage stores, ceramics shops, design studios, bookstores, and vinyl. The best walking shopping street in the city.
must_try: Browse Paxton Gate (oddities), Dog Eared Books, and the vintage shops.
hours: Varies by shop; most open 11 AM - 7 PM

name: Wasteland
description: High-end vintage and designer resale on Haight Street. Curated racks of vintage denim, leather jackets, and designer pieces. The Haight's best thrift stop.
must_try: Vintage Levi's and leather jackets.
hours: Mon-Sat 11:00 AM - 7:00 PM, Sun 12:00 PM - 7:00 PM

name: 1 Hotel SF - Bamford Wellness Spa
description: Eco-luxury spa at 1 Hotel open to non-guests. Organic Bamford products, treatment rooms with bay views. Book ahead.
must_try: Bamford signature body treatment.

name: Archimedes Banya
description: A Russian-style bathhouse in Bayview with hot rooms, cold plunge, outdoor deck, and restaurant. Co-ed. The most intense spa experience in the city.
must_try: Full banya circuit: steam room → cold plunge → repeat.

name: CorePower Yoga (Multiple Locations)
description: National chain with several SF locations offering drop-in heated and unheated yoga classes. First week free for new students.
must_try: Yoga Sculpt or Hot Power Fusion class.

name: Equinox Sports Club San Francisco
description: Premium fitness club downtown offering day passes for non-members via the 'E by Equinox' tier. Indoor pool, Hypervolt recovery, full spa.
must_try: Day pass with spa access and recovery suite.
hours: Mon-Fri 5:00 AM - 10:00 PM, Sat-Sun 7:00 AM - 8:00 PM

name: Kabuki Springs & Spa
description: Japanese-style communal bathhouse in Japantown. Hot pool, cold plunge, steam room, sauna. Alternating men's/women's/co-ed days. Deeply relaxing and authentically Japanese.
must_try: Communal soak + shiatsu massage

name: Ritz-Carlton Spa
description: Full-service luxury spa on Nob Hill open to non-hotel guests. Steam room, sauna, and a menu of massages and facials.
must_try: Deep tissue massage followed by the steam circuit.
